Theme 051 · Signature directions

Clean Product Film

The airy baseline: warm near-white paper, two soft colour clouds (teal for the fix, coral for the pain) and real product UI as the only “illustration”. Notification cards swarm the hook, the drop clears the frame to a calm lockup, and the proof is one honest window where a single row turns coral and a human presses Roll back.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Colour clouds — two blurred radial blobs (teal-soft + peach) that grow on the drop; never flat colour backgrounds
  • Notification card — white, r24, soft two-layer shadow, icon tile + bold title + mono meta; the hook’s crowd
  • Product window — one real-looking UI panel with a live dot; rows with sparklines = the proof surface
  • Anomaly row — coral left rule + tinted fill, mono “since · after” context line, primary + secondary action
  • Serif headline — Instrument Serif 76–108 px, exactly one italic teal word per frame
  • Coral pill CTA — the only solid coral object in the film besides the anomaly — pain and action share a colour

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Per-word headline — each word rises 24 px + fades, power3.out 0.35 s, one word per eighth-note (0.25 s at 120 BPM)
  • Beat-stagger cards — cards slide 60 px from alternating edges with 2–3° rotation, back.out(1.2) 0.5 s, one per beat (0.5 s)
  • Zoom-through seam — camera scales 0.6→1 into the window over one bar (2 s), expo.inOut; rows then fill one per beat and the anomaly lands on a bar downbeat

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

It is the version a buyer trusts first: no gimmick stands between the viewer and the product, so every beat reads on a phone in a muted feed. The risk is blandness — it lives or dies on typography, the shadow quality and cutting precisely on the beat; without the colour clouds it looks like a screenshot slideshow.

Adapt to your product: Swap the metric rows for your own product’s core list (tickets, invoices, builds, deals) and keep one row as the “problem” row with a context line and a single primary action. The cards in the hook are simply your users’ current tools and alerts.

References: https://m3.material.io/styles/motion/easing-and-duration (emphasized easing and duration scaled to distance) · https://linear.app/now/how-we-redesigned-the-linear-ui (calm, low-noise product UI as the hero) · https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2018/803/ (fluid, physically plausible interface motion)
